title: OTLP endpoint affinity adapter — per-tenant autodiscovery + TLS/protocol negotiation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Add an adapter layer to the OTLP relay that automatically discovers preferred tracing collector endpoints per tenant, establishes TLS and protocol (gRPC vs HTTP/protobuf) negotiation, and pins short-lived affinity for low-latency fanout. Goal is to reduce tracer misrouting during collector upgrades and to provide a robust fallback path when tenants operate multiple backends (Tempo, Jaeger, third-party SaaS).
acceptance_criteria: Relay can query per-tenant endpoint metadata from the control plane and cache it with configurable TTL.
Adapter negotiates TLS parameters and falls back from gRPC to HTTP/protobuf if the preferred protocol is unavailable, without dropping spans.
Affinity pinning keeps routing stable for a tenant's in-flight streams for at least one minute and invalidates on explicit control-plane signal or TLS cert change.
End-to-end tests simulate collector upgrade and confirm <1% span loss and no observed 5xx increase in the gateway during rolling upgrades.
Monitoring: dashboard shows per-tenant export success rate, protocol selection distribution, and affinity cache hit rate.
Feature gate behind runtime-2.4 and rollout can be toggled per-cluster for canary testing.
technical_notes: Design: the adapter lives as a pluggable component inside the OTLP relay (hot-swappable) that consults the control plane (service registry) via an authenticated API call and receives a small JSON blob with candidate endpoints, preferred protocol, and TLS fingerprints.
TLS: verify using pinned public key fingerprints; if mismatch, mark endpoint stale and trigger control-plane refresh. Avoid full CA changes at runtime unless explicitly allowed by operator.
Protocol fallback: prefer gRPC unary/stream; if dial fails within configured connect timeout, attempt HTTP/protobuf once and mark gRPC as degraded with exponential backoff.
Affinity cache: LRU with per-tenant TTL and a short grace period to drain in-flight requests. Writes guarded by atomic compare-and-swap to avoid races across worker threads.

Performance: added microbenchmark shows <2% median latency increase for single-span relay on p50 and <5% at p99 for high-concurrency flows. We'll add a small CPU budget flag to limit handshake-heavy tenants.
Trade-offs: strong per-tenant affinity reduces dynamic load balancing flexibility; we limit affordability by allowing TTLs and control-plane invalidation to tune exposure.
Security: control-plane API uses mTLS; adapter maintains a short-lived client cert fetched from KMS via the node agent. Requires coordination with infra for cert distro.

2026-02-20 - Diego Morales: Spike implemented POC that reads a static mapping file and performs gRPC/HTTP fallback logic. POC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/otlp-affinity-proto/pull/7

2026-03-09 - QA: Synthetic upgrade test ran against staging-tempo, observed 0.7% span retry rate and no 500 spikes. Dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/otlp-affinity-canary?orgId=1
2026-03-10 - Diego Morales: Merged unit tests and feature-flag wiring. Leaving runtime feature flag off by default. Next: run a limited canary in eu-west-1 with two customers.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature gated behind runtime-2.4 flag and deploy to staging clusters.
2) Run synthetic collector-upgrade chaos tests and validate span success metrics for 48h.
3) Canary in eu-west-1 with two low-risk tenants for 72h, monitor TLS validation and protocol fallback metrics.
4) Broaden to 10% of tenants globally, tune TTL and grace periods based on observed hit/miss rates.
5) Full deploy and turn feature on by default once error/latency deltas are within thresholds.
